text:
For an **overnight pellet-smoker cook**, I’d choose the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)**: its 2,073.6Wh capacity gives plenty of cushion, and its 2,600W inverter is well above the brief startup draw most pellet grills need. One estimate puts a 12-hour cook at roughly **450–750Wh**, so this station should cover more than one cook in typical conditions. [Source and estimate](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)

For a **single overnight cook on a budget**, a station around **1,000Wh** may be enough—but check your smoker’s startup requirements and allow extra capacity if you’ll also charge devices or run lights. Pellet grills draw a few hundred watts briefly to light, then typically much less while cooking. [Sizing guidance](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill)

Keep the power station dry and well away from grill heat, grease, and ash. If you mean an **electric smoker with a heating element**, that’s a much heavier load and needs a different, higher-output setup. [Difference explained](https://www.bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/how-long-can-bluetti-power-pellet-grill-smoker)
